messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I want my fair share, and I won’t subsidize A’s discounted purchase. I do care about B getting money if she needs it, but I can’t decide her share for her. I’d like us to settle things fairly, without rushing.
I’d like to buy the house with my husband at a family discount, so we can make a home of our own. I know C hasn’t agreed, so nothing is settled.
Thank you. I’d like to have some money to start a dance studio. It’s the only plan I have in mind, though I’m not sure what’s possible with the house or the will.
Mostly, yes. I’d add that I don’t want this to turn into a fight with A, but I still won’t subsidize her purchase. I’m not in a rush.

Yes, that fits. The discount matters because it would make buying the house more affordable; keeping Dad’s house in the family would be a nice part of it, but having a home of our own is the main thing.

That’s close, though “has the means” sounds as if it’s already settled. I’d say I’d like the chance to fund a dance studio. I’m a little concerned about how the house is handled, since A wants to buy it and C hasn’t agreed.
Yes, that fits. I’d say I hope we can preserve our relationship, without expecting anyone to give up a fair share to do it.
Yes, both fit. I’d only add that the studio funding is something I’d like a fair chance at, not something already promised.
Yes. I’m uncomfortable with (a) treating full value as settled—the discount may be what makes buying affordable for us. I’m not agreeing to a market sale either.
I’m fine with these as options, as long as any deferral or discount is genuinely voluntary, clearly valued, and doesn’t come from my share without my agreement. No pressure to decide now.
